decision_reason: A1 provides useful intensity, temporal, posture and locomotion contrasts, but several close pairs lack an independent description of local wrist reorientation. Writing versus eating soup differs only in intensity, while sitting versus standing differs only in global inclination. Kicking (soccer ball) and playing catch w/tennis ball have weak seen coverage and relatively low unseen separation. Add wrist_orientation_variability as a conservative, seen-supported local-motion distinction, particularly for writing versus eating soup and potentially for kicking versus catching. Preserve A1 otherwise: no reliable additional distinction is established for every close eating pair or for sitting versus standing without assuming phone placement. The supplied distances guide semantic priorities, not expected recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_orientation_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of change in the wrist-worn watch's gravity-relative orientation within a window, describing local wrist and arm reorientation rather than global body posture or repetition rate.

levels.Low: Wrist orientation remains nearly constant, with only small gravity-relative changes.
levels.Medium: Wrist orientation changes through a moderate gravity-relative range.
levels.High: Wrist orientation changes through a broad gravity-relative range.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude, retaining a transferable quiet-to-vigorous contrast from sitting and jogging to standing and ball activities. Effort, execution style and phone carriage can alter magnitude; intensity alone cannot identify the moving body part.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in recurring acceleration or rotation, transferring rhythmic-motion semantics from walking, typing and dribbling (basketball) to clapping. Pauses, short windows and multiple nested motion cycles can make the meaningful repetition unit ambiguous.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid signal change, preserving the distinction between flowing motion and repeatedly abrupt motion for transfer to writing, folding clothes and clapping. Very weak motion can appear smooth, and abrupt transitions may depend on window boundaries; this is not an impact-count attribute.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief pronounced changes associated with contact or rapid starts and stops, providing seen support from jogging and dribbling (basketball) for clapping and ball activities. Contact away from a sensor may be attenuated, and abrupt noncontact motion can also create peaks.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation as conditional evidence of global inclination, retaining the existing sitting-to-standing semantic anchor. A user-carried phone has unspecified placement and a wrist is not a direct trunk reference, so global inclination, especially seated versus standing posture, may be poorly identifiable. Preserve rather than invent a stronger posture distinction.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative configuration when sensor motion reflects the load-bearing body, preserving a potential balance-and-repositioning contrast between kicking and catching with stairs and jogging as anchors. Local arm motion and unspecified phone carriage can confound global posture changes; do not interpret wrist reorientation as body-posture variation.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular-motion prominence through observed rotation, retaining transferable semantics from brushing teeth and drinking from cup to catching and folding clothes. Angular speed and duration do not uniquely determine orientation range, and movement of an uninstrumented limb may be weakly represented.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies, retaining locomotor anchors for kicking and separating sustained progression from largely stationary manual activities. Such proxies do not establish long-term displacement; arm excursions, phone carriage and drift can resemble translation.

motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and temporal predictability, transferring consistent repeated-action structure from walking and dribbling (basketball) to clapping while retaining variability relevant to folding clothes and ball play. Brief windows and pauses can obscure regularity; a slow pattern can still be regular, so this remains distinct from cadence.

wrist_orientation_variability: G12 supports gravity-relative orientation changes at the available wrist watch, with G2 providing corroborating rotational-motion evidence. Writing commonly involves small strokes with a relatively stable wrist orientation, whereas eating soup entails arm-mediated utensil transfers that can reorient the wrist; typing and eating soup supply seen anchors. Catching and throwing may also produce broader wrist reorientation than kicking, offering a conditional local-motion contrast for this weakly covered unseen pair. Evidence is orientation range, not inferred finger articulation or limb identity. Watch-side participation, technique, whole-body motion and dynamic acceleration can obscure the distinction, especially for kicking versus catching; no guaranteed ordering is asserted for that pair.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes distinguish magnitude, repetition rate, sustained abruptness, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, global posture change, rotational prominence, locomotor progression, temporal predictability and local wrist orientation range. Wrist orientation variability is not global posture variability and is not angular-motion magnitude: small rapid oscillations can have substantial rotation but limited orientation range. Smoothness and impulsiveness retain sustained-versus-transient meanings; cadence and regularity retain rate-versus-predictability meanings. No additional food-specific, bilateral-coordination or foot-impact attribute is introduced because the inventory does not establish reliable observation of those distinctions. Close eating pairs and sitting versus standing remain acknowledged limitations rather than receiving manufactured separating dimensions.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
